Both versions are ready. They look and behave identically for saving and searching — the **only** difference is how a link relates to topics. Please open them one at a time and do the same small task in each, then tell me which fits how your mind works.

**Version 1 — a link lives in one topic (like folders):** http://maker:4001/topics-option1.html
1. Notice the row of topic buttons above the list. Click **Cooking** — the list narrows to cooking links. Click **All** to come back.
2. Save a new link, and when the details appear, type a single topic (e.g. `Reading`) in the **Topic** box, then save.

**Version 2 — a link can carry several topics (like labels):** http://maker:4001/topics-option2.html
1. Click the topic buttons the same way. Notice each link can show *more than one* topic; try clicking a topic tag *on a link itself* (e.g. the **Weeknight** tag) to filter by it.
2. Save a new link, and in the **Topics** box type one topic and press Enter, then another and press Enter — see that a link can hold several at once.

The thing I want your reaction to: **when you think of a saved link, does it belong in exactly one place, or is it natural for the same link to sit under several topics at once?** For example, a "quick weeknight chicken recipe" — is that only *Cooking*, or is it *Cooking* **and** *Weeknight*?

Which version matches how you'd want to organise — Version 1 (one topic each) or Version 2 (several topics allowed)?
